prompt: A hospital's revenue per patient fell 9% while patient numbers held steady. The share of patients on government insurance rose from 30% to 45%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Revenue per patient fell 9%, and government-insured patients rose from 30% to 45%.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: It could be the payer mix, coding, services offered, length of stay or billing.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: Government insurance is the problem, so the hospital should limit those patients.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: The shift toward government insurance, which pays less, likely explains most of the decline.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare revenue per patient by payer type.

explanation: A 15-point payer mix shift toward lower payers can explain a 9% drop. Revenue per patient by payer tests it.

distractor_flaws.M.restates_facts: Revenue per patient fell 9%, and government-insured patients rose from 30% to 45%.
distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be the payer mix, coding, services offered, length of stay or billing.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: Government insurance is the problem, so the hospital should limit those patients.
